domain: A do-while-shaped, five-state confirm/execute loop for the currently selected Inventory item or Psynergy ability against the polymorphic Data_03001f2c menu-runtime cell. State 0 clears the selection and primes the info window; state 1 waits a frame, checks the entry count, and (via a byte field at cell offset 0x268 that this draft calls `mode`) either assigns a shortcut and restarts or advances; state 2 classifies the selection through PsynergyMenu_ClassifySelectedPsynergy and either asks for confirmation (state 3), forces a self-target and executes (state 4), or finishes and writes the acting owner id plus the selection (masked 0x3fff) back through the caller's two out-parameters; state 3 re-confirms; state 4 actually calls the low-level ability-apply routine (Func_080a9f10, the same one games/gs1/src/item/use.c's Item_Use calls), pays the ability's PP cost from BattleAction.pp_cost via BattleUnit_Drain, recalculates the unit, plays the use animation or an error cue, and reports success/failure. The loop itself exits on a GameFlag_Test(0x150) check that is re-tested once more after the loop to force a -1 result.
expressed: the exact 5-state switch shape and its physical case layout (source order 0, 1, 3, 2, 4 -- confirmed by matching the reference's case-3-before-case-2 byte layout, not just its behavior)
the while-loop rotation (goto-condition-first) matching the reference's initial jump to the bottom-of-loop test block rather than straight into the switch

every real call target, argument, and struct-field offset touched (item_owner/target_owner @0x21a/0x21b, info_window @0x2c, the selected id @0x178 masked 0x3fff, entry_count @0x218, completion_flag @0x222, message_offset @0x25a plus (s32)&Value_00000bef, and the two not-yet-named fields at 0x24 and 0x268)

rejected_experiments.experiment: switch cases written in numeric order 0,1,2,3,4
rejected_experiments.result: wrong physical case layout -- case 3's body must precede case 2's in source for the compiler to lay out 0x13a before 0x162. Fixed; not reverted.

rejected_experiments.experiment: case 3 written as `if (x != -1) { state = 4; break; } else { ...; state = 1; }` vs the pre-set idiom `state = 4; if (x == -1) { ...; state = 1; }`
rejected_experiments.result: byte-identical candidate output either way -- the compiler normalizes both phrasings to the same pre-set-then-override shape. Kept the pre-set form for consistency with the rest of the function; not a residual lever.

rejected_experiments.experiment: local declaration order (result first vs last among the function's locals; result initialized before vs after state/done)
rejected_experiments.result: moving the declaration alone made no difference; moving the initializing *statement* ahead of state/done regressed to 317 candidate instructions (one extra) and a larger diff. Reverted to state=0; done=0; result=0 statement order.

rejected_experiments.experiment: case-4 locals (raw, self_flag, action) as a nested block-scope vs promoted to function scope
rejected_experiments.result: no change to the candidate output at all (same 316 insns, same 116-line diff, same fp/r9 residual). Kept the flatter function-scope form since it made no difference.
